acceptance: A unit test following the pattern of tests/unit/core/throughput/test_stream_timing.py asserts refresh_stream.start_monotonic is taken after the refresh connection factory returns and fails against the base commit when the factory sleeps.
The PR description states, with a code reference to the Ts computation, whether the refresh stream window affects Ts or Throughput@Size, and the changelog says so.
Refresh timing tests assert only what their names say; reviewer lists the tests read and the renames made.
uv run -- pytest tests/unit/core/throughput tests/unit/core/tpch/test_tpch_refresh.py passes.
docs/internal/tpc-measured-intervals.md row for the refresh stream window is updated and docs/internal/throughput-result-alignment.md still matches the code.
context: Origin: 2026-11-03 root-cause analysis of TPC-H RF1 timing (5 whys) and its adversarial review. Spec clauses cited here were read from the published PDFs at the links on 2026-11-03; re-read them rather than trusting this text.
description:
Problem. docs/internal/throughput-result-alignment.md states that a stream's window starts after its connection is open and ends before it is closed. The refresh stream does not follow that rule: in the TPC-H throughput refresh stream (benchbox/core/tpch/throughput_test.py, the method that sets refresh_stream.start_monotonic), start_monotonic and start_time are set before refresh_connection_factory() is called, so connection setup is inside the refresh stream window. Query streams take their start after the connection opens.

Change. Take the refresh stream's start after the connection is open; keep end_monotonic before the connection closes. Determine first, and record in the PR, whether the refresh stream's start or end participates in Ts (benchbox/core/throughput/runner.py compute_metrics, around the Ts span) or only the query streams do. If Ts changes, say so in the changelog; if not, say that only the reported refresh window changes.

Guardrails: Guardrails for all code work: work only in a linked worktree (make worktree-create); never edit the primary clone. No explanatory comments or docstrings in source (make comment-policy-check). Durations use benchbox.utils.clock.mono_time()/elapsed_seconds(). Add a changelog.d/ fragment. Cited line numbers are orientation only: re-read the named symbols, docs and spec clauses before editing and treat a mismatch as a reason to stop and update this item. No live-cloud runs without owner approval; heavy runs only through make heavy-run or a lock-taking entry point. Green focused tests are not release certification. Do not change what the RF1 and RF2 intervals themselves measure; that belongs to tpch-refresh-checks-timing-per-decision-20261103 and perf-tpch-rf1-bulk-load-20261031. Test names must say what they assert: rename any refresh-timing test whose name claims checks or connection setup are inside the measurement when the assertions say otherwise (tests/unit/core/throughput/test_tpch_refresh_timing.py and test_throughput_runs_all_safety_checks_outside_the_refresh_measurement in tests/unit/core/tpch/test_tpch_refresh.py are the places to read).
